name: Slack

verdict.headline: The app works in your own workspace right away and unlisted distribution needs no review, but any data-reading product effectively needs a Marketplace listing, which requires 10+ active workspaces before you submit and then up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks of review.
verdict.nextAction: Create the app at api.slack.com/apps, build OAuth v2, activate public distribution, and run an unlisted pilot to reach 10 active workspaces.

appType: Slack app with bot and/or user scopes, installed via OAuth v2. Distribute unlisted through Manage Distribution, or list it on the Slack Marketplace.

paths.name: Your own workspace only
paths.whenThisApplies: You only need the app in your development workspace. Install to Workspace gives a single-workspace token with no OAuth build.

timeline.label: Create the app, add scopes, Install to Workspace
timeline.note: Slack gives no figure for a single-workspace install. No review is involved.

paths.name: Unlisted public distribution
paths.whenThisApplies: You want other workspaces to install via an Add to Slack button or install URL, without a Marketplace listing. Commercial unlisted apps get Tier 1 limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies.

timeline.label: App, OAuth v2 and Activate Public Distribution
timeline.note: Hours to 1–2 days of build time. This is our estimate; Slack states no figure. No review is needed.

timeline.label: Workspace admin approval where a workspace requires it
timeline.note: Enterprise org installs and workspaces that require admin approval add friction. No time is known.

paths.name: Slack Marketplace listing
paths.whenThisApplies: You read Slack data at scale (unlisted commercial apps are throttled since May 29, 2025) or want to be listed. Requires 10+ active workspaces before submission.

timeline.label: App, OAuth v2 and public distribution
timeline.note: Hours to 1–2 days of build time. Our estimate; Slack states no figure.

timeline.label: Reach 10+ active workspaces
timeline.note: Active means used in the last 28 days. Time depends on your unlisted pilot.

timeline.label: Submission prep: landing page, privacy policy, support page, demo video, test accounts, scope justifications
timeline.note: Days to weeks. Our estimate; Slack states no figure.

timeline.note: Slack's stated maximum. Cannot be skipped or expedited.

timeline.label: Functional review (a reviewer tests the app and its scopes)

beforeApproval.item: The app works right away in your own development workspace.
beforeApproval.detail: Install to Workspace gives a single-workspace token with no OAuth build needed.

beforeApproval.item: Unlisted public distribution needs no review.
beforeApproval.detail: Activate Public Distribution gives an Add to Slack button, a shareable install URL and a meta tag.

beforeApproval.item: Unlisted commercially distributed apps: conversations.history and conversations.replies are Tier 1, 1 request/min, max 15 objects per call.
beforeApproval.detail: Applies since May 29, 2025 to new apps and new installs of existing unlisted apps. Internal apps keep 50+ requests/min and 1,000 objects. Marketplace apps are unaffected.

prerequisites.detail: Active means used in the last 28 days. You cannot submit to the Marketplace before this.

prerequisites.item: App type and category must be eligible
prerequisites.detail: Coded workflows are not eligible. Some categories are not accepted.

prerequisites.item: Public distribution activated and app publicly installable
prerequisites.detail: Manage Distribution checklist done: OAuth flow and SSL on every request URL.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps choose Create New App, From scratch or From a manifest (YAML/JSON). Pick a development workspace.
steps.agentHelp: Write the app manifest (YAML/JSON) with scopes and redirect URLs.

steps.title: Generate an app configuration token
steps.detail: Needed if an agent creates the app through the API. Config tokens expire after 12h; rotate them with tooling.tokens.rotate.

steps.title: Create the app via the manifest API
steps.detail: Call apps.manifest.create with the app configuration token.

steps.title: Add scopes and install to your workspace
steps.detail: Add bot scopes and/or user scopes. Install to Workspace gives a single-workspace token with no OAuth build.
steps.agentHelp: Pick the minimum scopes for the features that exist and add them to the manifest.

steps.title: Build the OAuth v2 handler
steps.detail: Redirect to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id, scope (bot), user_scope, redirect_uri and state. The returned code expires after 10 minutes; verify state. POST code, client_id and client_secret to oauth.v2.access. It returns an xoxb- bot token and, if user scopes were requested, an xoxp- user token under authed_user.

steps.title: Register redirect URLs
steps.detail: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS, have no #, and match (or be a subpath of) a URL registered in app settings. If several are registered, send the same redirect_uri in both steps.
steps.agentHelp: List the exact redirect URLs and add them to the manifest.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: In Manage Distribution, finish the checklist (OAuth flow, SSL on every request URL) and click Activate Public Distribution.

steps.title: Recruit 10+ active workspaces
steps.detail: Run an unlisted pilot until 10+ workspaces have used the app in the last 28 days.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications, privacy policy, support page and landing page
steps.detail: Justify each scope. Privacy policy covers what data is collected, use, retention, access/transfer/deletion, a contact, and data received but not used. Landing page is public with screenshots/GIFs and an Add to Slack path.

steps.title: Provide legal entity details and approve the privacy policy
steps.detail: The policy and listing need your legal details and sign-off.
steps.agentHelp: Draft the privacy policy for review.

steps.title: Run pre-submission checks
steps.detail: Automated pre-submission checks must pass. Remove test slash commands.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Cover install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Submit from the app's settings once eligible, with test credentials and dummy data.
steps.agentHelp: Prepare the submission checklist and scope justifications.

steps.title: Preliminary review
steps.detail: Slack reviews the listing, docs, scopes and installability. Up to 10 business days.

steps.title: Functional review
steps.detail: A reviewer tests the app and its scopes. Up to 10 weeks for new apps, up to 6 weeks for updates.

steps.title: Answer reviewer messages and staff support
steps.detail: Respond to reviewer messages, and to support requests within 2 business days.

steps.title: Workspace admin approval
steps.detail: Workspaces that require admin approval, and Enterprise org installs, need an admin to approve the install.

submissionChecklist.item: App fully functional, publicly installable, and tested on a non-dev workspace
submissionChecklist.detail: Test install, onboarding, use and uninstall.

submissionChecklist.item: No test slash commands left in

submissionChecklist.detail: No scopes for features that don't exist yet. Avoid legacy, restricted or broad scopes (admin.*, search:read, triggers:*).
For your service and any third-party service it connects to.

submissionChecklist.item: Install path that doesn't need your workspace

submissionChecklist.detail: Covers install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall.
Public, not a PDF or repo, with screenshots/GIFs and an Add to Slack install path.

States what data is collected, how it's used, how long it's kept, and how users can access, transfer or delete it. Includes a contact email or form and discloses data the app receives but doesn't use.
An email or form that doesn't require an account. Respond within 2 business days.
TLS 1.2+, signing-secret verification (verification tokens are deprecated), state in OAuth, tokens never logged or exposed.

submissionChecklist.item: No training LLMs on Slack data
submissionChecklist.detail: AI agent apps must not store Slack data.
Includes AI fields: model, retention, tenancy.

gotchas.title: Rate-limit cliff for unlisted commercial apps (May 29, 2025)
gotchas.detail: conversations.history and conversations.replies dropped to Tier 1: 1 request/min, max 15 objects per call, for new apps and new installs of existing unlisted apps. Internal apps keep 50+ requests/min and 1,000 objects; Marketplace apps are unaffected. Any data-reading product effectively needs a Marketplace listing.

gotchas.title: Existing unlisted installs are not throttled
gotchas.detail: Slack's current changelog says the Tier 1 limits "will not be applied to existing installations" of unlisted apps. An earlier version of the page set dates for existing installs (September 2, 2025, later March 3, 2026), but those dates have been removed. Only new apps and new installs are throttled.

gotchas.title: Updated ToS dates
gotchas.detail: The updated ToS took effect immediately for apps created on or after May 29, 2025, and on June 30, 2025 for older apps.

gotchas.title: 10 installs before you can submit
gotchas.detail: You need 10 active installs before submitting, so plan an unlisted pilot phase.

gotchas.title: Resubmitting in preliminary review resets your queue position
gotchas.detail: Resubmitting during functional review does not reset it.

gotchas.title: Review cannot be skipped or expedited
Broad scopes get enhanced review
gotchas.detail: Apps with broad history or private-channel scopes get enhanced review.

gotchas.title: Slack may security-review the app at any time
Turning off distribution uninstalls the app everywhere else
gotchas.detail: It uninstalls the app from every other workspace. Once the app is listed, you must discontinue the listing instead.

gotchas.title: Direct-install URLs must 302-redirect
gotchas.detail: They must redirect to a full oauth/v2/authorize URL.

gotchas.title: Short-lived codes and config tokens
gotchas.detail: The OAuth code expires after 10 minutes. App configuration tokens expire after 12h.

blockers.whatToDo: Send the same redirect_uri in the authorize and oauth.v2.access steps, and make sure it is HTTPS, has no #, and matches (or is a subpath of) a registered URL.

Check the common reasons: app in beta or untested, bugs that block testing, scopes for features that don't exist yet, legacy/restricted/broad scopes, missing or inaccessible test accounts, incomplete submission, earlier feedback not addressed.
The app is an unlisted commercial app under Tier 1 limits. Get it listed on the Marketplace.
Check estimated timing and reviewer messages on the Marketplace submission page, then contact Slack developer support. There is no stated SLA and review cannot be expedited.
